title: Pixel art with Claude
author: maarkeez
selftext:
Hello fellow ai-coders!

I would like to create pixel art for my game. I tried using Opus 5.5 and its raw tools (python scripts mostly) and the results were kind of bad. 

I want it to create character and environment sprites for a top down game with a look and feel similar to a Link to the past. The sprite size will be somewhere between 16-32px.

I know there is an aseprite mcp and I would like to know 

\- Did any of you tried it? How was the experience?  
\- How does your prompts look like?  
\- Any useful skill worth mentioning?  
\- What other alternatives are available? 

As far as I am aware, Claude model strengths do not include image generation. I do not want charming pixel art for now, just something acceptable. I am open to hear about other models in other platforms, although if possible would like to know about alternatives using Claude to do not increase my pet project costs.

Thank you all beforehand!

comments.author: Free-Version-2746
comments.body: throw link to the past sprite sheet to claude and tell claude to mimic it.

replies.author: maarkeez
replies.body: I already did that and the results were not much better 😅🙃

comments.author: klas-klattermus
comments.body: I recently bought aseprite for the mcp and it works alright, maybe I need to learn it better but it's at least better than what Claude does without any tools

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body: Claude doesn't have image gen. Use a different tool

comments.author: flavorfox
comments.body: I have and in my experience it’s not good enough. Best workflow for me, at the moment, is create art in codex from prompts dwscribing style in 96x96 - be sure to make it use sinple shapes otherwise it wont downscale, create tools and workflows for palette and snapping. And the clean up in hand.

comments.author: Hitom52
comments.body: I recommend Pixellab. For a while, I tried to find ways to save money because I really can't afford to create a game. But after seeing the results, hiring an artist has always added more value to the game.

comments.author: FazedEclipse2
comments.body:
You need your AI to build from Blender and render down.

You have two ways to do this from here, you can generate a 3d model that looks similar to what you want and render those down, or have it built in Blender.

Claude is very very poor at the build part.

Codex is very very good at building them.

comments.author: Limp_Bus3865
comments.body: just use a tool mad for image gen why are you overcomplicating this

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body: I've been messing up a lot with Claude for pixel art, it can generate [great pixel art scenes](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/opus-5-5-for-pixel-art-scenes) as well as very good for code-driven FX. For pure sprites & animations, I use Sprite Fusion.

replies.author: maarkeez
replies.body: That was a nice example! Thanks for the blog post

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Yes, it was a solid 10mn thinking from Claude, though x) But I'm pretty sure it will be much shorter in the next model cycle.
